key_insight: Expandable modality experts support strong medical image–text representation learning while preserving existing representations when new imaging modalities are added.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support medical image classification and image–text retrieval across modalities, but clinical utility and patient outcomes were not evaluated.
method: Combine shared visual computation with modality-routed experts and a separate text pathway.
Pretrain on unpaired images, then align image and text embeddings using paired data.
Add fundus and OCT experts while freezing existing image and text embedding paths.
evidence_signal: Using 19.4 million unpaired image rows and 3.23 million image–text pairs, the ViT-Large model achieved best or tied-best results in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities.
watch_item: Representation preservation depends on unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions; retention checks cover evaluated inputs rather than all possible deployment data.
paper_title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
